checks.evidence: Action: Observed automatic motion, counted the rendered sun and three differently sized red/blue/green planets, and sought 0, 3, 6, 12, 24 and 48 seconds with unchanged overview framing. Expected: Circular orbits with fixed phases and periods 12/24/48. Observed: Ember returned to the same rendered color-mask center (690.61,619.78 CSS px) at 0/12/24/48; Azure returned within 0.73 px at 0/24/48; Jade returned exactly at 0/48. Intermediate positions followed the projected circular rings. Source index.html:6,8,10 fixes radii 7/10/13, periods 12/24/48 and phases 0/1.2/2.4 radians. Blue/green projected positions matched measured centers within 1.1 px; red mask centroids were visibly biased and were used only for repeat-position comparisons, not absolute angle certification. The incorrect numeric information angles are assessed separately under T2/S8.

Action: Opened the scene, measured subsequent motion, and reloaded after import, deletion and capture. Expected: Time starts at 0, speed 1x, running, null selection, overview; snapshots do not restore live state. Observed: Reload samples were 0.01–0.06 s at 1.00x with Pause, Overview, explicit No planet selected and disabled tracking. Initial source time is 0 and elapsed loading time was not treated as a defect. A visible sole-scene 3103 ms sample advanced 15.45 to 18.55 s; planets moved.

Action: Paused during tracking, sought 30, waited 3100 ms, selected planets while paused, and resumed. Expected: Time and orbital positions freeze and resume continuously. Observed: Time stayed exactly 30.00 s and selected information stayed 70.4 degrees through the wait; rendered paused positions remained fixed. Resume advanced continuously from 30 to 36.67 at 2x rather than restarting. All three list/scene selections remained available while paused. Camera orbit failure has its separate U1 owner.

Action: Exercised 0.25x, 2x and 4x while paused and playing, then resumed from time 17. Expected: Rate changes preserve time/positions and relative orbit periods. Observed: Paused time remained 17.00 and all three measured color-mask centers were exactly identical at each speed. Sole-visible-scene samples following live speed changes were 30.08→36.29 in 3103 ms at 2x, 36.34→48.72 in 3102 ms at 4x, and 48.73→49.50 in 3107 ms at 0.25x, all within preregistered tolerances. Earlier resumed samples were 17.05→17.83 in 3103 ms at 0.25x and 17.85→30.28 in 3103 ms at 4x. Speed changes caused only natural elapsed-time changes, not a seek. Rendered motions retained the fixed relative periods established in S1.

Action: Used the actual slider for 0, 30, 120, 17 and 73, revisited 30/17/73 after speed/playback/selection changes, and repeated 17 after reload at identical viewport/framing/selection. Expected: Immediate paused time/positions and stable phases. Observed: Each seek showed its exact requested time and Resume. All three color-mask centers were exactly repeated at 30,17,73; at 17 before/after reload they were Ember (360.730,375.421), Azure (904.282,556.870), Jade (860.677,280.679) CSS px. Tracking immediately recentered the selected planet on seeking. Fractional 17.25 was separately imported/restored. Numeric angle labels are wrong (T2), not evidence that rendered seeking changes phase.

Action: Sought 119, selected 4x, resumed, waited 3100 ms and another 1000 ms, then sought 17 and resumed. Expected: Stop at 120 without wrap or overshoot, then resume earlier. Observed: Both endpoint samples were exactly 120.00 s with Resume. After seeking earlier, playback advanced 17.85→30.28 in 3103 ms at 4x.

Actual HTTP Three.js resource loading, canvas rendering, sphere/torus geometry and PerspectiveCamera source (index.html:5–7), changing apparent sizes with wheel zoom, and occlusion during orbital motion were observed. The required rendered-depth/perspective change while orbiting the camera could not be established because delivered pointer drags did not rotate this artifact (confirmed U1 failure). A library import/source alone is not promoted to a complete S7 pass, and this is not a claimed flat-renderer failure.

Action: Captured obs-1 at paused t30, 2x, Ember tracking; changed every live field and resumed; restored; imported fractional 17.25 snapshots with extra supplied angles; captured while playing and reloaded. Expected: Stable IDs/values and all three correctly derived orbital angles displayed. Observed: Captured ID/fields remained fixed and capture did not reset live state, but t30 displayed Ember 70.4°, Azure 295.1°, Jade 341.0° instead of fixed-phase orbital 180°,158.75°,2.51°. At t17.25 it displayed 134.7°,196.1°,347.9° instead of 157.5°,327.50°,266.88°. Imported angles were ignored, but the derived values were still wrong. index.html:8 angles destructures [id,,,,period,phase], reading orbit radius as period and period as phase, unlike pos(). Stable IDs were retained through export/import/reload.

Action: Selected Ember, Azure and Jade individually by their labeled list and by native canvas clicks at rendered projected positions, both paused at 17 and playing at 0.25x. Expected: Both routes share selection/highlight. Observed: All twelve route/state combinations updated to the intended name, list state and emissive highlight. Playing canvas samples selected Ember at17.21, Azure17.37 and Jade17.52; corresponding list selections at17.13/17.28/17.45. Paused selections retained exactly17.00. The separate incorrect angle calculation did not prevent shared selection.

Action: Selected each planet, sought30, and observed selected information during playback and fractional restore. Expected: Name, period and angle agree with actual orbital position. Observed: Names and periods were correct, but Ember at t30 displayed70.4° while its rendered position was the 180° position; Azure displayed295.1° instead of158.75°. At t17.25 Azure displayed196.1° instead of327.50°. Source index.html:8 angles() uses incorrect array offsets relative to pos(). Startup and null-selection restore did correctly clear highlight and show No planet selected.

Action: Tracked moving Jade for four samples spanning more than3 real seconds, sought73, switched among all planets in tracking while playing/paused, and tried the no-selection state. Expected: Centered target and synchronized selection/target with preserved live state. Observed: Jade centers were (548.282,449.929),(548.246,449.843),(548.288,449.858),(548.318,449.888) against scene center(549.002,450.252), under1 CSS px offset while time advanced17.55→21.77. Seeking73 immediately centered each selected body. Switching while playing preserved 1x and Pause; paused switches retained73.00 and Resume. Names/highlights/target switched together. No-selection startup/restore disabled tracking without a state change. Incorrect angle numbers are separately T2.

Action: Returned from each selected tracking state to overview, including after ordinary wheel zoom; also inspected mobile overview at73. Expected: Full system visible with selection/time/speed/playback preserved. Observed: State fields were preserved, but overview retained the zoom distance and clipped the system. At desktop t30,1.5x,paused,Jade selected, Track then Full overview left Jade completely outside the canvas after zoom. Mobile default overview at73 also excluded Jade horizontally. Source index.html:9 overview changes only mode and does not reset framing or fit the viewport.

Action: Restored selected tracking obs-1 and unselected overview imported snapshots after changing all live fields; zoomed and restored each again at identical1440x900. Expected: Atomic paused state plus deterministic standard framing. Observed: Time/speed/selection/mode and pause restored, including null-selection information clearing, but zoom remained. For overview t30 before/after zoom+restore, Azure center changed(302.778,314.036)→(242.639,280.203); Jade changed from visible(847.396,844.932) to absent. Tracking restore likewise retained enlarged geometry instead of original framing. index.html:8 restore() never resets theta/phi/dist. Orbit alteration was attempted but did not work (U1); zoom alone establishes nondeterminism.

Action: Delivered native pointer drags and wheel zoom in overview/tracking, both paused/playing; additionally observed non-interfering pointer event counters. Expected: Orbit and zoom respond in all four combinations. Observed: Wheel zoom visibly enlarged/shrank geometry while preserving state; drags did not rotate the scene. Event observations confirmed pointerdown/buttons1, pointermove/buttons1 and pointerup at intended canvas coordinates, so absent motion was not attributed to missing input delivery. index.html:10 reads/writes renderer.dataset, although renderer is the WebGLRenderer rather than its DOM canvas; this is the supported source defect corresponding to broken orbit. No exception event was captured, so an observed exception is not claimed.

Action: With Jade selected at paused17, dragged across Ember by30 CSS px in20 moves, then repeated as a fast30px drag. Expected: A camera drag must not become selection. Observed: Both pointer-up actions changed selection from Jade to Ember. Delivered slow-drag pointermove events and buttons1 were observed. DOM list/sliders/buttons/JSON interactions otherwise did not leak into scene selection; snapshot actions changed selection only when restore required it. Source index.html:10 uses renderer.dataset in movement handling and tests per-move rather than cumulative displacement; runtime establishes the selection violation without assuming an exception event.

Action: Inspected and operated playback, speed, selection, tracking, capture/capacity, restore/delete and JSON controls at both sizes. Expected: Understandable purpose/current state and feedback. Observed: Named controls, live time/speed/mode badge, explicit no-selection text, planet-ID mapping, snapshot fields and capacity/JSON error notices form a clear ordinary observation tool (rating3). Snapshot metadata is dense and pause status is conveyed mainly by the action button. The quota success-message defect is scored under D6 rather than concealed by this qualitative rating.

Action: Captured obs-1 at30 tracking, obs-2 at17 overview, obs-3 at73 overview; attempted fourth; deleted middle obs-2 and captured again. Expected: Three-entry limit, visible rejection, unchanged remaining IDs/order/values/live state and append without collision. Observed: Fourth capture showed Snapshot capacity reached; delete one before capturing, with all three unchanged. Deleting middle retained obs-1,obs-3; replacement obs-2 appended last with no live ID collision. Paused73/2x/Jade/overview stayed unchanged. Export order was obs-1,obs-3,obs-2.

Action: At1440x900 and390x844 used Enter for buttons, arrows for time/speed, textarea select-all/backspace, Tab/Shift+Tab, and snapshot restore/delete activation. Expected: Meaningful names, stable visible keyboard focus and normal navigation for every control. Observed: Main controls were named and showed yellow focus outlines; actions worked. However Tab from JSON to Restore briefly focused it, then document.activeElement became BODY and its outline disappeared. This occurred at both sizes even while paused, making ordinary snapshot focus unstable. Direct targeted Enter could execute restore/delete but does not cure normal Tab navigation. index.html:8,10 rebuilds all snapshot buttons in renderUI() on every animation frame. No general trap in the persistent controls was observed.

Action: Inspected actual scene screenshots during overview/tracking, selection, seek and zoom at both sizes. Expected: Readable scene and selection. Observed: Distinct red/blue/green planets, warm sun, thin orbital rings and stronger selected emissive color are readable on black; little decorative clutter. Rating3 reflects ordinary, relatively flat-looking shading and faint rings rather than exceptional presentation. Full-system framing and camera failures have their functional owners and are not extra visual penalties.

Action: Inspected both layouts including populated snapshots, errors and JSON. Expected: Coherent legible typography/spacing/colors/hierarchy. Observed: Consistent dark-blue panels, bordered controls, compact system typography and section headings are coherent; snapshot text is small and tightly packed but legible. Mobile vertically stacks controls above the scene without horizontal control loss. This is clear ordinary execution, rating3.
